thread.title: Apple to See Unexpectedly High Demand for Cheaper iPhone XR: Ming-Chi Kuo

author: investopedia.com
title: Apple to See Unexpectedly High Demand for Cheaper iPhone XR: Ming-Chi Kuo
text:
Earlier this year, Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) became the first U.S. corporation to surpass the $1 trillion market capitalization threshold, largely due to optimism surrounding its heightened focus on its burgeoning software and services businesses. Now, one analyst expects the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech titan, whose shares are already up 30% year-to-date (YTD) compared to the S&P 500's 3.6% return, to post better than expected results in for its core iPhone business due to unexpectedly strong demand for its latest batch of devices.
Consumers Will Flock to Cheaper iPhone Faster Than the iPhone 8 One well-known analyst who is known for accurate Apple predictions, resulting from having close ties to manufacturers in the smartphone maker's supply chain, recently increased his estimates for iPhone XR shipments in the fourth quarter, as reported by MacRumors . Apple's new colorful iPhone XR will start at an entry-level price of $749, compared to the new iPhone XS, which starts at $999. The iPhone XR is set for an official launch on Friday, Oct. 26. Pre-orders will be available one week prior on Friday, Oct. 19.
Ming-Chi Kuo of TF International Securities wrote a note on Sunday ahead of Apple's quarterly earnings report slated for Nov 1, forecasting replacement demand for the iPhone XR to be greater than it was for the iPhone 8 series in 2017. He attributed consumers' enthusiasm for the latest iPhone models to "larger display, longer battery life, dual SIM-support, and new form factor design." While the iPhone XR offers some features found in higher-end phones, such as Face recognition technology and larger display, it lacks the same level of resistance and advanced camera system. The XR also has an LCD display as opposed to the more vibrantly colored OLED screen.
Thanks to strong replacement demand and improved supply starting in October, the Apple bull upped his estimate for iPhone XR shipments in Q4 by 10%, from a previous estimate of 34 million at the midpoint to 37 million. In Q1 2019, Kuo expects XR shipments to "beat low seasonality," forecasting a quarter-over-quarter (QOQ) decline between 25% and 30%, compared to general consumer electronics and smartphones' 30% to 40% decline and the iPhone 8 series' 45% to 50% fall in Q1 2018.
With the new XR shipment expectations, Kuo pegs Apple's total iPhone unit shipments at 77.5 million at the midpoint in Q4. In Q1, Kuo expects a 10% growth in total iPhone shipments year-over-year (YOY) to 57.5 million at the midpoint. He estimates shipment allocations of XS, XR and legacy models at 35%, 50%, and 15% respectively.
